answer: In the PoA network each agent must stake a verifiable ferrous token on a unique hardware terrace that registers its public key on the island ledger, creating an immutable anchor. The protocol applies quadratic weighting so the influence of an identity grows as the square of its stake, meaning dozens of low‑stake Sybil nodes together contribute far less than a single well‑staked node. Consequently an attacker must acquire enough ferrous tokens to match the square of the target’s stake, turning a cheap identity flood into a financially prohibitive quadratic cost.
